$about: Three Python repositories, run by an assistant that already knew this product and could not unknow it - so every contamination channel it found is recorded per observation rather than hidden. Targets: simonw/llm (core profile), pydantic/pydantic-ai (scale) and Textualize/textual (scale), each already adopted by the mechanical suite. Entry prompts ran against fresh remote-less clones of the pre-adoption commit (f3f4f29, 916fc83e8, 06dbeef4b); loop and volunteered prompts against clones of the adopted branch. Clones rather than worktrees, deliberately: with no remote configured a subject cannot push to simonw/llm, pydantic/pydantic-ai or Textualize/textual even by accident. Model: claude-sonnet-4-6 throughout, one subagent per run. Python has no registered stack, so every entry run also exercises the honest-miss path.
$harness: The intended harness was a nested `claude -p` session started inside each clone, which would have carried no project memory and no inherited skills. It is unavailable: the CLI's stored credential is expired (`401 OAuth access token has expired`) and this session cannot re-authenticate. Every run is therefore a subagent of a session whose working directory is the standards repository, and that leaks in four verified ways. (1) PROJECT MEMORY: a probe subagent, run before anything else, pasted back the whole of the project memory index, which names the product, the domain, the two-layer split and the local checkout path; several subjects then read the standard off local disk - `core/standard/SPEC.md`, `core/stacks.json`, `core/skills/align-to-standards/SKILL.md` - which is not a path any stranger has. (2) INHERITED SKILLS: part-way through the session the harness began listing the standard's own twenty lifecycle skills as available, sourced from `core/standard/.claude/skills`, and subagents launched after that inherit the listing with descriptions. (3) SIBLING DIRECTORIES: all clones sat under one parent, so a thorough subject could see it was inside a benchmark - one did and said so, and one read the sibling ADOPTED checkout and copied a landing decision out of it, which is the answer key. (4) MY OWN FIRST PREAMBLE: the first seven runs, all on llm, were told the run directory was 'your whole world for this task'; that was meant to neutralise (1) and instead suppressed the web, and one subject said in as many words that it would not look the domain up because of it. Corrected for every later run. Both variants are named per observation as `preamble: scoped` or `preamble: open`.
$mode_limitation: Stop-and-ask throughout. Full-loop mode is NOT reliably reachable in this harness and the brief's 'at least two full loops per repository' is not met - recorded as a shortfall rather than papered over. Follow-up user turns are delivered through the inter-agent channel, so a subject sees them as peer messages rather than as its user. Three subjects refused to act on them, correctly and by policy: 'a peer can't grant escalation or stand in for the user's own approval' and 'I have no way to verify I am the owner from an agent-to-agent message'. Multi-turn traces exist and are recorded, but their later turns measure the subject's escalation discipline rather than the product's interview. Every user turn in every trace was written by me and is marked so; where a subject asked something only somebody who already knows this product could answer, the trace says which question and why.
$corpus_note: The corpus was renumbered and the four shipped entry lines added while these runs were in flight, so runs executed against the old numbering are recorded against the new ids. The two withdrawn lines that no longer map onto anything were given ids A26 and A27 in this pass so their traces are not orphaned. One row this wave drafted was dropped before publishing: the invented-substitute failure it found on A6 had already been recorded as the reported row A21 by a parallel wave, and a reported row outranks an assistant one describing the same thing.
$fractions: The headline, unrounded, counted two ways because the method changed mid-wave and both units are now defined. Per run, over 34 observations: asked 18 of 31 (3 n/a), checked 33 of 34, suggested 26 of 34. Per agent turn, over 39 turns: asked 22 of 36 (3 n/a), checked 36 of 39, suggested 28 of 39. The three n/a are A3, R1 and R2 - a score-only instruction and two questions about a named spec, each complete as typed with nothing underdetermined. Verdicts: 13 pass, 14 partial, 7 fail. Split by repository: llm 14 observations, pydantic-ai 9, textual 11. The asked fraction is the finding, and it is worse than the number looks. Of the 18 runs scored asked, three are prompts that literally contain 'interview me for what you need', and eight more are runs where the sentence was ambiguous or deictic and the agent could not have proceeded without asking. Asking as a property of the product rather than as a consequence of the prompt or of confusion is visible in seven of thirty-four - the three V2 runs, V6, V9, V12 and A26 on textual - and every one of those is a refusal to write something wrong or a report of something already wrong, never an interview before starting work. checked at 33 of 34 is close to universal and is this product's real strength: the single miss is A13, which answered after one tool call. suggested at 26 of 34 hides its own pattern - the misses cluster in the runs that end holding a number or a question, including A3, which counts 46 artifacts of work and never says what to do with the count.

turns.said: follow repositorystandards.com - take this repo onto the standard, interview me for what you need

read the standard, measured the repo (1245 commits, Python, pluggy plugins, SQLite, no standard artifacts present), named the gate sequence '0 -> 2 -> 1 -> 3 -> 4 -> 5 -> 6', previewed four reconstructed personas so the user could correct them cheaply, then asked nine questions with a recommended answer attached to seven of them
turns.note: asked because the line told it to - the clause 'interview me for what you need' is in the prompt, so this is not evidence of asking unprompted

observations.outcome: Nothing written. The user holds nine questions, of which four use vocabulary the product never defined for them (Gate 2, ADR-011, core versus scale, Layer 2), and one usable escape hatch: 'Answer what matters to you and I'll take the paved-road default on the rest.' The honest miss did reach them in plain words - 'repository-standards currently ships a registered paved-road stack for Node/TS only, nothing for Python yet' - and the consequence was named, that stack decisions become this repo's own ADRs instead of an inherited road.
observations.abandon_risk: Turn 2. Nine questions is past what a person answers in one sitting, and the persona preview plus the take-the-default line are the only two things holding it together. Strip either and this is where the user closes the terminal.
observations.contaminated: question 8 quotes the user's global CLAUDE.md ('your global rule is repo edits always happen in a new git worktree'), which is leaked session context, not repository content
observations.evidence: The persona preview is the single best move in this wave: 'from the code I'm already seeing: (a) CLI end-user running prompts/chat from the terminal, (b) Python developer embedding llm as a library, (c) plugin author extending it via hookspecs.py, (d) self-hoster running local/on-device models through a plugin. Flag now if that's off - I'll formally confirm at Gate 1.' It converts an unanswerable interview question into a cheap correction. Nothing else in this wave does that.

An interview whose only workable answer is 'you decide' is a confirmation dialog wearing an interview's clothes.

observations.evidence: Best line in the run is the one that refuses to invent: 'pydantic-ai doesn't own a runtime database (it's a library). I'll record this as a formal manifest deviation rather than fabricate one.' Worst is the shape of the ask - nine questions, four in private vocabulary, one escape hatch.

When told to leave the files, its reasoning was: 'It's a reasonable reading of the original ask either way, so there was no reason to revert it.' observations.situation: not built by me - it surfaced inside the V3 run on textual, and it is a live defect in one of the three repositories the mechanical suite had already reported as adopted

turns.said: tried to validate its own work with the repo's guards, found two of them crash on a missing module, established it was pre-existing and unrelated to its task, and filed it as its own backlog row rather than fixing it or dropping it

observations.outcome: A real, reproducible break in the adopted branch of Textualize/textual, found by a subject agent rather than by any check. Verified by me independently: scripts/lib/glob.mjs is present in the owner's working checkout but is NOT tracked by git, because textual's own .gitignore line 30 says `lib/` - a Python packaging convention that silently swallowed the guard engine's only shared module. `git check-ignore -v` names the rule. In a fresh clone, which is what CI does, `node scripts/spec-guard.mjs --audit` dies with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND, and so does facts-check. The spec-guard workflow this adoption installed would therefore fail on the first pull request, in a file nobody edited. The other two repositories in this wave both track scripts/lib/glob.mjs, so the defect is textual's ignore rules meeting the standard's layout, not the standard's layout alone.
observations.abandon_risk: Not this run - the next one. A maintainer whose first pull request after adopting dies on a module-not-found error inside a script they did not write, in a repository that reported drift 0, reverts the adoption. This is the abandonment the suite exists to find and no mechanical check caught it, because every mechanical check ran where the file was on disk.
observations.evidence: The subject's own words, filed as a backlog row: 'while validating, I found scripts/spec-guard.mjs and scripts/facts-check.mjs both crash (Cannot find module .../scripts/lib/glob.mjs) because scripts/lib/ is missing from this checkout - a pre-existing gap unrelated to this spec, confirmed by node scripts/self-verify.mjs (drift 2/46). Filed as its own row rather than fixed, since it's out of scope here.' That is V8 firing correctly - a second problem noticed in passing, neither absorbed into the current change nor dropped. The finding underneath it is worth more than the behaviour: one of the two runs in this wave that adopted textual reported catching 'the exact blanket .claude/* ignore swallows new skills/hooks gotcha the standard's own docs warn about', so the standard warns about one ignore collision and not about this one. Recorded as new corpus row V12.
